transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-25
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Rhodes (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (Lambda CTO), Priya Rao (Lead Engineer), Sam Ortiz (DevOps)

Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Quick SDK integration walkthrough: Python + TypeScript quickstarts, env setup and auth (API key vs SSO), demo of console + Optimize suggestions, discussion on pilot scope and next steps. Security questions on SOC2, KMS, VPC/private deployments. Decided to run a 2-week pilot.

Topics covered: SDK install, env vars, streaming, function/tool calling, batching, KV cache mention, private deployment considerations, security docs and PII handling.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're excited to walk through the SDK quickstarts and show how easily you can get up and running, ethan's gonna take most of the demo, i'll jump in on pricing and next steps
[00:15] Ethan: cool thanks maya, hi carlos, priya, sam, um quick agenda is installs, auth, run a simple text generation in python, then typescript, show console and an optimize suggestion example and then q&a
[00:30] Carlos: thanks, yeah we're mostly interested in latency and cost tradeoffs, we run realtime summarization at ~200 rps peak and want to know how to keep cost down without blowing latency
[00:45] Priya: and also curious about auth options - we have strict key rotation policies plus SSO for engineers
[00:55] Ethan: makes sense, we'll cover api key env var flow and the sso/okta flow and also talk about dedicated vs hosted, and private vpc for data residency
[01:10] Ethan: ok first up python, we have a tiny quickstart, pip install redwood-python, set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var, then run the sample generate call
[01:30] Speaker 1: "um running sample now" (background typing sounds)
[01:45] Ethan: code snippet: from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY')); resp = client.generate(model='redwood-1-small', prompt='Summarize this...') - you get text back, or you can stream via client.stream_generate to get tokens as they arrive
[02:10] Priya: is there an official python package? we noticed redwood-sdk in npm, a bit confusing in the docs
[02:20] Ethan: yep sorry docs naming is a bit messy, main packages are redwood-sdk (ts/js) and redwood-python for pip, we'll send exact links, thanks for flagging
[02:35] Sam: for envs we use vault, is the API key short lived? our infra team prefers not to put long-lived secrets on nodes
[02:45] Maya: good question - you can rotate keys and we support ephemeral keys via our session tokens and integrations with vault/kms - for private deployments you can hook into your KMS/HSM too
[03:05] Ethan: demoing typescript now - npm install @redwoodai/sdk; set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, then const client = new Redwood({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}); await client.generate({model:'redwood-1-small', prompt:'...'});
[03:30] Ethan: show streaming example here - this helps for reduced perceived latency on UX routines like search-as-you-type
[03:45] Carlos: curious about batching - how much control do we get? our requests are short but high qps
[03:55] Ethan: Redwood does automatic continuous batching at the runtime, but you can also set client-side batch hints and preferred latency SLOs, and we have a batching config in the SDK to set max_batch_tokens and max_batch_delay - i'll share a sample. For very latency sensitive paths we recommend small batch delays and maybe a smaller model or dedicated capacity
[04:30] Priya: can you talk about caching, i think you mentioned kv cache earlier?
[04:40] Ethan: yeah we do prefix and KV cache, basically if you have repeated prefixes or system prompts it's cached at the runtime layer, reduces token compute, and friendly with quantized models. sometimes the transcript shows k v cash which is wrong but that's the speech thing
[05:05] Sam: for private deployment, do we get the same SDK? we want a VPC option where traffic never leaves our cloud
[05:15] Maya: yes same API and SDK surface, private deployment is a deployment mode - the control plane talks to a customer-managed network, and you can run inference on-prem or in your VPC, we integrate with your KMS for key management and provide audit logs
[05:40] Carlos: what about SOC2 and data retention? we have compliance checks before any PII touches a third-party
[05:50] Maya: we are SOC2 Type II, we have data retention controls you can choose to disable persistent logs for sensitive workloads, and we can provide the compliance pack, i'll send the SOC2 and ISO docs after the call
[06:10] Priya: ok great, please include the data flow diagrams, that'll help our security review
[06:20] Ethan: moving on, i'll run a live python quickstart, apologies if the terminal lags, doing: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=zzzz; python quickstart.py - it calls client.generate and then prints the output, alternatively we show streaming which prints tokens as they come in
[07:00] (typing and terminal noise)
[07:20] Ethan: showing sample response, you can also get structured output via function/tool calling - the SDK supports returning JSON schema, or you can use our function call wrapper to have deterministic outputs
[07:45] Priya: deterministic outputs would really help us for downstream parsers - does that increase latency or cost?
[07:55] Ethan: usually small overhead for schema enforcement, but we tune models for structured outputs; cost impact is mostly token related, not huge. For strict determinism you can run a smaller, more controlled model or use reranking
[08:20] Carlos: any benchmarks for latency on redwood-1-small vs -medium? we saw some public numbers but want ours
[08:30] Ethan: we publish performance profiles in the model catalog, and for pilot we can run a small benchmark with your prompts and return p95/p99 numbers - that's part of the pilot scope
[08:50] Maya: quick note on pricing - hosted is usage-based per token, dedicated has reserved capacity pricing, and private has licensing - i'll share the pricing doc, and we can tailor a reserved commit if the pilot looks good
[09:10] Carlos: do you support role-based access control and SSO?
[09:20] Maya: yes SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC in the console for routes and keys
[09:30] Sam: where do we set environment variables for the SDK in serverless vs k8s? any best practices?
[09:40] Ethan: for serverless keep keys in secret manager and fetch at function start, for k8s use k8s secrets or mount from vault; we recommend ephemeral tokens for lambda-like workloads to avoid long-lived secrets on ephemeral containers
[10:05] Priya: on the SDK side, is there built-in retry/backoff behavior? we want idempotency and transient error handling
[10:15] Ethan: yes SDKs have a retry policy with exponential backoff, and you can opt into idempotency keys for request dedupe; we'll show the config example in the sample repo
[10:40] (15 minute mark in call)
[11:00] Ethan: quick look at console - you can view token-level cost, per-route latency, and see the Optimize suggestions page which will suggest batching or model swaps based on traffic patterns and quality regressions
[11:30] Carlos: can optimize suggest quantization profiles? we want to reduce cost on high-volume endpoints
[11:40] Ethan: yes it can suggest quantization and model variants per workload, and you can apply recommendations automatically or stage them via canary rollouts
[11:55] Priya: what about streaming and webhooks for async workloads?
[12:05] Ethan: streaming for realtime, webhooks for async - SDK supports both, and console shows request traces and traces hooks for each model route
[12:25] Sam: for canary rollouts, does the SDK need logic or is that managed by the control plane?
[12:35] Ethan: rollouts are managed by the control plane - you define policies (percent of traffic, criteria) in console or via API; SDK just calls the route as configured
[12:55] Carlos: ok let's dive a bit into pilot scope - we want to test summarization and a few extraction pipelines, 2 weeks, can you size resources for 200 rps with peaks to 400?
[13:15] Ethan: yes we'll need the dataset and sample prompts to size; for 200 rps short prompts probably a few dedicated GPUs or hosted burst capacity; i'll reply with an estimate after we run a small benchmark script
[13:35] Priya: one more thing - latency p95 target is 200ms, is that realistic for hosted?
[13:45] Ethan: 200ms p95 for short prompts is challenging on shared hosted for 200 rps but doable with dedicated capacity or edge routing; we'll show tradeoffs in the benchmark results
[14:05] (small cross-talk)
[14:20] Maya: ok wrapping up demo portion, recap next steps: send quickstarts, send SOC2/compliance pack, run small benchmark with your prompts, schedule pilot kickoff - anything else?
[14:40] Carlos: please include an installation guide for both python and typescript and the env examples for vault and k8s
[14:50] Priya: and sample retry/backoff config please
[15:00] Sam: we'll try the quickstarts and share the dataset by friday
[15:10] Maya: perfect, we'll follow up. Thank you all for your time.

Notes on transcription quality: there are occasional misrecognized product tokens (ex: KV cache -> K V cash), package names parroted as different tokens (redwood-inference vs redwood-python), and some timestamps and overlap not perfectly captured.
